text:
- [LLEX.12.1] **`_` is optional, for every unit** (LUNI.3.1.1). A unit
  literal is `NUM_PREFIX _? UNIT_SUFFIX`: `30_s` and `30s` are one
  token, as are `100_km` / `100km`, `23_°C` / `23°C`, and — `45°` / `45_°`, `30′`, `45″`. The plane-angle
  glyphs are ordinary `UNIT_SUFFIX` characters. Within the numeric prefix, `_` before a digit is a group
  separator (`23_000_m` = `INT_LIT(23000)` then unit `_` then
  `UNIT_SUFFIX(m)`); the separator before the suffix is the unit `_`.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__digits_run
idris.note: The clause's separator rule in a parsed `INT_LIT`: within the numeric prefix a `_` before a digit is a group separator, so a `_` is admitted where a digit follows and nowhere else -- not at the end of the run, not before another `_`.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__refused_spellings
idris.note: The trailing separator `31_` parses to `null`, executed; the unit `_` before a suffix (`31_s`) is no part of an `INT_LIT` and parses to `null` too.
